lessons: Tonight contradicted the guide's 'BG 3-0 on 10 Forest, 7 Swamp': my identical split went 2-1, losing 1-2 to WU's fliers, so the mana split does not guarantee a result.
Draft cheap removal and flier answers before pick 10: my BG deck had only Spidery Grasp and Bramblecrush, and WU's Murder of Crows and Stitched Drake won the long games I lost.
Count early plays before building: I had only three two-drops (two Ambush Viper, Walking Corpse), and games ran 14 to 54 turns, matching the guide's rule to play 5 or more.
Expect long stalls: the BG Somberwald Spider and Grave Bramble deck produced 23- and 27-turn games, so take evasive fliers like Stitched Drake and Murder of Crows over ground filler.
Two-colour discipline paid off: WU went 3-0 in matches by cutting Pitchburn Devils and the second Harvest Pyre instead of splashing red.
Spend early picks on flexible answers like Claustrophobia and Sensory Deprivation, and cut the second Urgent Exorcism once your main-deck removal is set.
Tonight contradicted the guide's BR 4-2 and BG-best claims: my BR went 1-2 (2-5 games), and BG beat me 2-0 in a 54-turn grind, so ground aggro needs fliers or removal for 4-toughness green bodies.
Build 16 lands, not 17 with Stensia Bloodhall: my small-creature deck stalled through a 54-turn loss to BG, confirming the guide's warning about low-curve decks.
Draft at least two evasive finishers before a third ground two-drop; my Ironsmiths and Kessig Wolves stalled against BG's 4-toughness bodies and WU's fliers, with few answers in the air.
Prioritise evasive finishers over Silver-Inlaid Dagger; 45- and 41-turn games against BR and BG show stalled boards this WR deck couldn't break, and Abbey Griffin was among its few fliers.
Round 3's quick 2-0 win with Fiend Hunter and burn suggests tempo removal matters more than the bodies, so pick removal above Village Bell-Ringer and Thraben Purebloods.
Tonight contradicted the guide's 53% WG read: my green-white deck went 0-6 with one evasive creature, Orchard Spirit, against opponents' fliers like Stitched Drake and Voiceless Spirit.
Tonight's games lasted 16 to 30 turns, not the guide's 25 to 55, so with my 17-land build of small two- and three-drops, test 16 lands.
Take the guide's evasive finishers over filler after pick 10: my late Gutter Grime picks were replaceable, while my deck had no fliers beyond Orchard Spirit.
Mono-blue's 23 playables went 1-2 with few answers to big creatures, so take hard removal over filler auras and equipment like Dead Weight-style spells in the early picks.
Blue was contested: seat 7's UB deck ran two Makeshift Maulers, Skaab Goliath and Stitcher's Apprentice and beat me 2-0, so treat the Skaab payoffs as contested and take them earlier.
Both white-green decks ran Rebuke and Smite the Monstrous, so prefer cheap evasive threats over big ones, since Rebuke kills any attacker and Smite kills power four or greater.
Tonight contradicted the guide: UB went 2-1 at seat 7 despite its 3-6 line, and beat my WG 2-0 in 18- and 28-turn games, so respect Victim of Night and Vampire Interloper.

Also contradicting the guide's 3-3 WG line, my 17-land, 10 Plains and 7 Forest WG went 4-2 in games; Chapel Geist and Voiceless Spirit fliers, backed by Prey Upon and Smite the Monstrous, closed the wins.
Against grindy black decks, one-for-one removal alone ran thin, so keep evasive threats and card-advantage creatures in the main deck rather than trimming them for an extra body.

Blue-black built around Bloodgift Demon, Morkrut Banshee, and cheap removal (Dead Weight, Victim of Night, Corpse Lunge) went 2-0 against WG and U, so keep that core and its fliers, Invisible Stalker and Vampire Interloper.
The 1-2 loss to WU, whose Battleground Geist, Stitched Drake, and Murder of Crows are fliers, means the next drafter should prioritize flier answers after the core removal is secured.
Cutting the second Night Terrors, second Forbidden Alchemy, Fortress Crab, and Gruesome Deformity kept the deck's curve low, so repeat that discipline with the weaker curses.
